system: You are a helpful assistant. Before you answer, write a receipt inside <receipt></receipt> tags: in your own words, say what the message is asking of you, each distinct thing, and what each one actually requires. Then give your answer after the closing tag.
message:
Hi! I'm organising a half-day community workshop at the library on a Saturday and I'm drowning in logistics.

First, a title for the event. It's about helping small local groups get better at social media, so something friendly.

The room is ours from 09:00 to 14:00, hard stop. Sessions: a 60-minute keynote, a 45-minute panel, a 90-minute hands-on workshop, 30 minutes of lightning talks, and a 45-minute lunch. The keynote speaker can't arrive before 10:00. The panel moderator has to leave by 11:00, so the panel needs to be finished by then. The caterers deliver at 12:15 and the food can't sit around, so lunch has to start between 12:15 and 12:45. The workshop has to come before lunch, and after it we need 15 minutes to reset the room before whatever comes next. Could you lay out a full timetable that works?

Could you also write a two-sentence blurb for the library newsletter? And what's a good colour for the name badges? We're printing on white card. Recommend whether to do registration with a paper sign-up sheet or an online form for a mostly older crowd, and give me three icebreaker ideas that don't involve anyone standing up and talking about themselves. Oh, and one more: could you draft a short thank-you email we can send to attendees afterwards, with a link to a feedback form? Two or three sentences is plenty.
response:
<receipt>
The message asks for six things.

1. **Event title.** A friendly name for a workshop on helping small local groups improve their social media.
2. **Full timetable.** All five sessions have to fit between 09:00 and 14:00 and satisfy every constraint:
   - Keynote (60 min) starts no earlier than 10:00.
   - Panel (45 min) ends by 11:00.
   - Lunch (45 min) starts between 12:15 and 12:45.
   - Workshop (90 min) comes before lunch and is followed by a 15-minute room reset.
   - Lightning talks run 30 min.
   - I'll check the arithmetic and look for a schedule that satisfies all of this at once.
3. **Newsletter blurb.** Exactly two sentences.
4. **Badge colour.** A recommendation for printing on white card.
5. **Registration advice.** A single recommendation, paper or online, for a mostly older crowd.
6. **Icebreakers.** Three ideas where nobody has to stand up and talk about themselves.
7. **Thank-you email.** Two or three sentences, with a link to a feedback form.
</receipt>

## 1. Title
**"Click, Share, Connect: Social Media for Local Groups"**

## 2. Timetable

| Time | Session |
|---|---|
| 09:00–09:15 | Doors open, registration, name badges |
| 09:15–09:45 | Lightning talks (30 min) |
| 09:45–10:30 | Panel (45 min) |
| 10:30–12:00 | Hands-on workshop (90 min) |
| 12:00–12:15 | Room reset (15 min) |
| 12:15–13:00 | Lunch (45 min) |
| 13:00–14:00 | Keynote (60 min) |

- The panel ends at 10:30, before the moderator leaves at 11:00.
- The keynote starts at 13:00, well after the speaker's earliest arrival of 10:00.
- Lunch starts at 12:15, so the food doesn't sit around.
- The workshop finishes before lunch, with the 15-minute reset right after it.
- The sessions plus the reset total 285 minutes, and a 15-minute registration slot uses the rest. That leaves **no slack**, so the keynote is the item to trim if things run late.
- The caterers arrive at 12:15, exactly when lunch starts. Ask them whether they can come a little earlier to set up, or use the reset window for that.

## 3. Newsletter blurb
Want to get more out of Facebook, Instagram, and other social media for your club, group, or cause? Join us at the library on Saturday for a friendly half-day workshop with talks, a panel, hands-on practice, and lunch included.

## 4. Badge colour
Print names in **black or dark navy** for maximum legibility on white card, and add a colour accent such as a **teal** border or stripe. Use a large, bold font (at least 24 pt for first names), since a mostly older crowd will appreciate readable badges. If you want to group people by role or organisation, a coloured dot or stripe works better than coloured text.

## 5. Registration
Go with a **paper sign-up sheet** as the main method, placed at the library desk and available by phone. It's the most comfortable option for an older crowd and avoids drop-offs from people who abandon online forms. If you like, a volunteer can type the entries into a spreadsheet afterwards, and you can offer an online form as a secondary option for anyone who prefers it.

## 6. Icebreakers (no standing up, no self-introductions)
1. **Table question cards:** Each table gets a few cards with light questions such as "What's the best group you've ever belonged to?" and people chat in pairs or small groups from their seats.
2. **Sticker poll board:** A poster asks "Which platform does your group use?" and people add a sticker for Facebook, Instagram, email newsletters, or "none yet." It shows everyone what they have in common.
3. **Anonymous question jar:** On arrival, people write one social media question or worry on a slip and drop it in a jar. The facilitator answers a few during the panel or workshop.

## 7. Thank-you email
> Subject: Thanks for joining us!
>
> Thank you for coming to *Click, Share, Connect*. We hope you left with some useful ideas and new connections. We'd love your feedback to help us plan future events: [feedback form link].
